name: Coleman-De Luccia Bubble
description: The spacetime of a false vacuum decaying, found by Sidney Coleman and Frank De Luccia in 1980. A bubble of lower vacuum energy appears by quantum tunnelling, its wall accelerates outward toward the speed of light, and the inside of the bubble is an open universe with no singularity at its start.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ and $G$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Can a universe rest in the wrong vacuum? Think of water heated past its boiling point in a very clean pot: it sits there, liquid and overdue, until one bubble of steam forms and grows [coleman1977, coleman1980]. A field theory can be stuck the same way, with two stable homogeneous states of different energy density, and the upper one, the false vacuum, decays by tunnelling through the barrier between them [coleman1977]. By 1974 Mikhail Voloshin, Igor Kobzarev, and Lev Okun had studied the bubbles of such a metastable vacuum, and by 1977 Sidney Coleman, joined by Curtis Callan for the quantum corrections, had the semiclassical theory of the decay [voloshin1974, coleman1977, callan1977]. A bubble of true vacuum appears at rest, and then its wall, a thin skin between the two vacua, runs outward along a hyperboloid, closing in on the speed of light [coleman1980].¶Does gravity care? At first glance no, wrote Coleman and Frank De Luccia in 1980, since a bubble forms on scales where gravity is "utterly negligible" [coleman1980]. Its growth is another matter [coleman1980]. A bubble releases energy in proportion to its volume, and its Schwarzschild radius grows in step, catching up with the bubble's own radius at the length $(8\pi G\epsilon/3c^4)^{-1/2}$, with $\epsilon$ the difference in energy density between the two vacua [coleman1980]. For a difference of $(1\,\mathrm{GeV})^4$ that length is 0.8 kilometres, a scale they called "civic, or even domestic" [coleman1980]. Without gravity the zero of energy means nothing, and with gravity it is a cosmological constant, so each vacuum has its own and the wall parts two different spacetimes [coleman1980].¶The bubble they built has the most symmetry it could have: the tunnelling solution is assumed round in four Euclidean dimensions, which leaves a single unknown function, the radius $\rho(\xi)$ of the 3-sphere at distance $\xi$ from the centre [coleman1980]. They warned that no theorem backs the assumption, and that if a lopsided solution of lower action exists, "all our conclusions are wrong" [coleman1980]. Turn one of the four directions into time and the rotations become Lorentz transformations about the event where the bubble appears [coleman1980]. Outside that event's light cone the spacetime is a stack of hyperboloids of radius $\rho(\xi)$, and the wall stays on one of them, since the symmetry allows no other kind of surface [coleman1980]. Inside the light cone $\xi$ turns into a time and each hyperboloid into a space of constant negative curvature, so that "the interior of the bubble always contains a Robertson-Walker universe of open type" [coleman1980].¶Two cases had special interest for them, because the cosmological constant observed today was zero as far as anyone could tell, and Stephen Parke later did the same for any pair of vacua [coleman1980, parke1983]. If our vacuum is what a decay left behind, the inside of the bubble is Minkowski space, the outside is de Sitter space with $\rho = \ell\sin(\xi/\ell)$, and no bubble is born wider than the de Sitter radius $\ell$ [coleman1980]. If our vacuum is the false one, the bubble holds anti-de Sitter space, and its negative energy curves space until a large bubble has too little volume for its surface, so below a certain energy difference no bubble forms and gravity has stabilized the false vacuum [coleman1980]. The open universe inside has the scale factor $\ell\sin(c\tau/\ell)$, and Coleman and De Luccia argued that even tiny corrections turn its return to zero, a time $\pi\ell/c$ after the start, into a true singularity [coleman1980]. Five years later Larry Abbott and Coleman proved the collapse for bubbles that are not perfectly symmetric [abbott1985]. Vacuum decay was already "the ultimate ecological catastrophe", and the one comfort left, that the new vacuum might sustain "some structures capable of knowing joy", went with it: "This possibility has now been eliminated" [coleman1980].¶Could we be living inside one? In Alan Guth's inflationary universe of 1981 the expansion was meant to end by this kind of decay, and with Erick Weinberg he showed two years later that the bubbles never merge into one smooth region, however much of space they fill [guth1981, guth1983]. A year after Guth's paper J. Richard Gott took a single bubble for the whole observable universe, an open one with no singularity at its start [gott1982]. The idea needed a second, slow stage of inflation inside the bubble, which Martin Bucher, Alfred Goldhaber, and Neil Turok supplied in 1995 [bucher1995]. An infinite open universe fits inside a bubble of finite size because its moments of constant cosmic time are the hyperboloids inside the light cone, each one infinite [bucher1995]. Once string theory seemed to have a vast number of vacua, Ben Freivogel, Matthew Kleban, María Rodríguez Martínez, and Leonard Susskind argued that our universe was born in such a tunnelling event, which would make it open [susskind2007, freivogel2006].¶To someone who stays put, in the static coordinates of either vacuum, the wall is one curve $r_w(t)$, and Steven Blau, Eduardo Guendelman, and Guth, and Victor Berezin, Vadim Kuzmin, and Igor Tkachev, used those coordinates in 1987 with Werner Israel's junction conditions to follow the motion of thin walls [blau1987, berezin1987, israel1966]. The opposite bubble, false vacuum inside true, looks like a black hole from outside while its inside inflates into a closed universe that disconnects from the original spacetime [blau1987]. Edward Farhi and Guth showed that such a bubble, once past a critical size, must have begun at a singularity, "an insurmountable obstacle" to making a universe in the laboratory [farhi1987]. A neighbouring bubble that hit ours would leave a mark on the microwave sky, and in 2011 Stephen Feeney, Matthew Johnson, Daniel Mortlock, and Hiranya Peiris found that the WMAP data "do not warrant" adding such collisions to the standard cosmology [feeney2011]. Our own vacuum may be the false kind: for a Higgs boson lighter than 126 GeV, absolute stability of the Standard Model's Higgs potential is excluded at 98% confidence, by the 2012 calculation of Giuseppe Degrassi and his collaborators [degrassi2012].

related.text: The inside of a bubble whose new vacuum has zero energy. With $a = c\tau$ the open universe inside is Milne's, flat space in hyperbolic slices [bucher1995].
The false vacuum of positive energy outside the wall, written around the bubble's centre with $\rho = \ell\sin(\xi/\ell)$ [coleman1980].
The inside of a bubble whose new vacuum has negative energy. Coleman and De Luccia argued that the smallest disturbance makes it collapse [coleman1980].
The side of the wall where the vacuum energy is zero: the inside of the bubble if our vacuum is what a decay left behind, the outside if ours is the false one [coleman1980].
The inside of every bubble is an open Friedmann universe, $k = -1$, and its $a = 0$ is the light cone of the bubble's centre, a coordinate singularity [coleman1980, bucher1995].
A thin wall with the same flat vacuum on both sides. Its world volume is a hyperboloid as well, de Sitter space of three dimensions [caldwell1996].

A de Sitter space whose earliest region is a loop in time. Gott and Li have bubbles like these forming in its inflating region, and in their fuller scenario a baby universe born in one of them is the de Sitter space the bubbles formed in [gott1998].

Coleman's bounce carried from a false vacuum to the whole universe: half a 4-sphere joined at its equator to the waist of a closed de Sitter universe, which Vilenkin had created from nothing [vilenkin1982].

coordinates.name: Outside the Light Cone
domains: \xi = 0 \;\text{(the light cone of the bubble's centre)}

parameters.description: Radius of curvature of the hyperboloid at $\xi$, a length, zero on the light cone $\xi = 0$, where $\partial_\xi\rho = 1$. In a vacuum of cosmological constant $\Lambda$, with $\ell = \sqrt{3/|\Lambda|}$, it is $\xi$ for $\Lambda = 0$, $\ell\sin(\xi/\ell)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, and $\ell\sinh(\xi/\ell)$ for $\Lambda < 0$. Across a thin wall of surface energy density $\sigma$, on the hyperboloid of radius $\bar\rho$, $\rho$ is continuous and $\partial_\xi\rho$ drops by $4\pi G\sigma\bar\rho/c^4$

coordinates.convention: We use Coleman and De Luccia's coordinates outside the light cone of the event the bubble is centred on: $\xi$ is the proper distance along the curves of constant $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$, zero on that light cone, and $\psi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$ are coordinates on the hyperboloid of events at one $\xi$. The rapidity $\psi$ is a pure number, itself the chart's $x^0$, and we leave the function $\rho(\xi)$ free. In the geodesic equations a dot is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Open Universe
domains: \tau = 0 \;\text{(the light cone of the bubble's centre)}

parameters.description: Scale factor of the open universe inside the bubble, a length, zero on the light cone $\tau = 0$, where $a' = 1$. In a vacuum of cosmological constant $\Lambda$, with $\ell = \sqrt{3/|\Lambda|}$, it is $c\tau$ for $\Lambda = 0$, $\ell\sinh(c\tau/\ell)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, and $\ell\sin(c\tau/\ell)$ for $\Lambda < 0$, which returns to zero at $c\tau = \pi\ell$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, \chi, \theta, \phi)$ inside the future light cone of the event the bubble is centred on, with $\tau$ the proper time since that light cone along the comoving world lines and $\chi$ a rapidity, a pure number. We leave the scale factor $a(\tau)$ free. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, a prime is the derivative along that chart time, $a' = da/d(c\tau)$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{\tau}$ means $d(c\tau)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Open Universe, Conformal Time
domains: \eta \to -\infty \;\text{(the light cone of the bubble's centre)}

parameters.description: Scale factor of the open universe inside the bubble, a length. In a vacuum of cosmological constant $\Lambda$, with $\ell = \sqrt{3/|\Lambda|}$, it is $\ell e^{\eta}$ for $\Lambda = 0$, $-\ell/\sinh\eta$ on $\eta < 0$ for $\Lambda > 0$, and $\ell/\cosh\eta$ for $\Lambda < 0$

coordinates.convention: We use the conformal time $\eta$ of the open universe inside the bubble, a pure number with $a\,d\eta = c\,d\tau$ for the proper time $\tau$ of the comoving world lines, and the comoving $\chi$, $\theta$, and $\phi$. The conformal time is itself the chart's $x^0$, and we leave the scale factor $a(\eta)$ free. A prime is $d/d\eta$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Static, Inside the Wall

parameters.description: Cosmological constant of the true vacuum, inside the wall, of either sign, carrying an inverse length squared

Areal radius of the wall, a length, with $r_w^2 = \bar\rho^2 + \left(1 - \Lambda_T\bar\rho^2/3\right)\tanh^2\left(\sqrt{\Lambda_T/3}\,ct\right)/(\Lambda_T/3)$ for a wall born at rest with the radius $\bar\rho$ at $t = 0$; that is $\bar\rho^2 + c^2t^2$ at $\Lambda_T = 0$, and the hyperbolic tangent is a tangent for $\Lambda_T < 0$

coordinates.convention: We use the static coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of the true vacuum about the bubble's centre, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Static, Outside the Wall

parameters.description: Cosmological constant of the false vacuum, outside the wall, of either sign, carrying an inverse length squared

Areal radius of the wall, a length, with $r_w^2 = \bar\rho^2 + \left(1 - \Lambda_F\bar\rho^2/3\right)\tanh^2\left(\sqrt{\Lambda_F/3}\,ct\right)/(\Lambda_F/3)$ for a wall born at rest with the radius $\bar\rho$ at $t = 0$; that is $\bar\rho^2 + c^2t^2$ at $\Lambda_F = 0$, and the hyperbolic tangent is a tangent for $\Lambda_F < 0$

coordinates.convention: We use the static coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ of the false vacuum about the bubble's centre, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
